name: Pennywise
label: Epitaph
lede: Four Hermosa Beach kids who played backyard parties wrote a song for three dead friends. Its writer died in 1996, the singer quit and came back, and the band kept going for thirty-plus years.

eras.title: Backyard parties, then Epitaph
eras.text: Four South Bay kids start as P.M.A. and play beach-town parties. Two EPs and a signing to Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph make them a label pillar.

years.h: Four Hermosa Beach kids start P.M.A.
years.p: [[Jim Lindberg|430709c6-32a6-4829-83d6-0a794e7de31c]], [[Fletcher Dragge|0426363b-f0a6-4e2a-a467-d32efbed08a4]], Byron McMackin and Jason Thirsk form the band in 1988. All but McMackin went to Mira Costa High School.
years.xp:
P.M.A. stood for Positive Mental Attitude, and the band worked the beach-town party circuit around Hermosa. Thirsk on bass wrote many of the earliest songs.

The name Pennywise comes from Stephen King's novel It. Wikipedia quotes the band saying they took it from the book, not the film.

yt: Bro Hymn, live at Gampel Open Air 2006
years.h: Thirsk writes Bro Hymn for three friends he lost
years.p: Tim Colvin, Carlos Canton and Tom Nichols are the three. Nichols drowned off Hermosa Beach Pier in 1988.
years.xp:
Canton died in a motorcycle accident, per Wikipedia.

Lindberg later pointed to the song as the reason the band couldn't stay split: "You can't have a song like 'Bro Hymn' which is about friendship, unity, and sticking with your friends and then have a total fracture in the middle of the band."

yt: Full early set, North Hollywood Theater, 1990
years.h: Two EPs come out before any label shows up
years.p: A Word from the Wise and Wildcard are the band's own releases, ahead of a deal.

years.h: Epitaph releases the first album, with Bro Hymn on it
years.p: Brett Gurewitz of [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]] runs the label. He signed the band in 1990, per Wikipedia, and Pennywise follows a year later.

years.h: Lindberg quits six months in
years.p: He cites a lack of motivation and security in local rock bands. He's back by late 1992.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives no dates beyond the six months and the late-1992 return, and sources on the gap are thin.

eras.title: Lindberg comes back
eras.text: Lindberg rejoins in late 1992 and the band settles in. About Time is their first Billboard 200 entry.

years.h: Lindberg returns, Bradbury plays bass for a stretch
years.p: Thirsk moves to vocals for a time in 1992 while Randy Bradbury joins on bass. Bradbury leaves, then returns for good in 1996.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Bradbury as bassist in 1992 and again from 1996. Sources on the exact shape of the 1992 shuffle are thin.

years.h: Unknown Road, the first album of the second run
years.p: Lindberg is back at the mic, and the record arrives on Epitaph in August 1993.

yt: Live at Alternative Nations, Sydney, April 15, 1995
years.h: About Time is the first Billboard 200 entry
years.p: It peaks at number 96, and at number 55 on Australia's ARIA chart, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: After Thirsk
eras.text: The bassist dies in July 1996. The band keeps playing, dedicates Full Circle to him, and becomes a Warped Tour regular.

years.h: Jason Thirsk dies at 28
years.p: He had been in rehab for alcoholism and had suffered from depression. Wikipedia reports he died by suicide from a gunshot wound.
years.xp:
Thirsk was born December 25, 1967, in Hermosa Beach. His girlfriend found him about a day after his death, per Wikipedia.

The band dedicated its Warped Tour 1996 shows to him.

years.h: Bradbury takes the bass for good
years.p: He replaces Thirsk in 1996 and is still in the job.

yt: Full show, Warped Tour LA, July 3, 1997
years.h: Full Circle is dedicated to Thirsk
years.p: The band re-record Bro Hymn as Bro Hymn (Tribute), with his brother Justin on drums and vocals for the track.
years.xp: The album also carries Thirsk's lyrics, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Straight Ahead, the fifth album
years.p: Epitaph again, three years after the band's bass player died.

years.h: A drunk Dragge blocks the Loveline studio door
years.p: The 6-foot-5 guitarist, in for a KROQ Weenie Roast promotion, keeps hosts Adam Carolla and Dr. Drew from leaving. Police show up. No charges follow, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the incident to June 1999 and says Dragge threatened violence while the hosts were held in the studio.

years.h: Gurewitz co-writes Who's on Your Side
years.p: Land of the Free? has the Epitaph boss's name on one track, and the band plays Vans Warped 2001.

eras.title: Albums, charts, a free download
eras.text: From the Ashes is their highest initial chart entry, and a free MySpace download in 2008 draws over 400,000 downloads.

years.h: From the Ashes debuts at number 54
years.p: That's the band's highest initial chart position, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The Fuse lands in Europe first
years.p: Europe gets it June 27, 2005. North America waits until August 9.

years.cap: Pennywise on stage at a club show, February 2007
years.h: Pennywise gives Reason to Believe away on MySpace
years.p: Wikipedia counts over 400,000 downloads. The album also reaches number 98 on Billboard.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the free release one of the band's most successful. It came out March 25, 2008.

years.h: Reason to Believe is the ninth album
years.p: It's the record that went out free first.

eras.title: A singer leaves, another comes, the first returns
eras.text: Lindberg walks away to make a documentary and a side band. Ignite's Zoli Teglas steps in, then a back injury reopens the door.

years.h: Lindberg leaves to make a movie
years.p: He quits in August 2009 and forms the Black Pacific while filming The Other F Word, based on his book Punk Rock Dad.
years.xp: The documentary follows punk rockers who became dads. Release dates differ by source, so none is given here.

years.cap: Pennywise live in Rio de Janeiro, December 2010
years.h: Ignite singer Zoli Teglas gets the job
years.p: The Orange County hardcore vocalist is announced as Lindberg's permanent replacement.

years.h: Teglas sings on one record: All or Nothing
years.p: It's the only Pennywise album with him on it, out May 1, 2012.

years.h: A back injury in Germany ends Teglas's run
years.p: He needs emergency surgery and asks to leave. That opens the door for Lindberg to come home.

years.cap: Lindberg at Rock im Park, June 2014
years.h: Lindberg announces his return on KROQ
years.p: He says he wanted the fighting to stop. The band couldn't play a song about unity and be fractured down the middle.
years.xp:
Lindberg told LA Weekly: "I just wanted what was going on to stop."

He also blamed e-mail. "We started having our problems when e-mail became the primary source of communication," he said, "the worst way for bands to do business." His summary of where it stands: "I think we've hugged it out."

eras.title: Back in the backyard
eras.text: A Palladium run marks 25 years, and Yesterdays goes back to the earliest Thirsk-era songs.

years.h: Twenty-five years, a Palladium run, and a family reunion
years.p: Lindberg says the Hollywood Palladium shows brought enormous relief that the family was back together.
years.xp: He compared the split to a divorce: "people feel like they have to pick sides." "It was rough for all of our friends in the area," he told LA Weekly.

years.big: "We didn't care about anything except playing backyard parties."
q: We didn't care about anything except playing backyard parties and having fun.
years.h: Yesterdays reaches back to the backyard-party days
years.p: Many of the songs are Thirsk's, written before 1996, and the sound is deliberately plain. Epitaph releases it July 15, 2014.
years.xp: Lindberg called the songs "very unambitious" and said the last couple of records the band made together were overproduced: "We got pasteurized somewhat." His plan this time: "mic the instruments, sing until your voice is raw, and put it out!"

yt: Bro Hymn, live at Punk Rock Holiday, 2019
years.h: Never Gonna Die is album twelve
years.p: Dragge, McMackin, Bradbury and Lindberg all play on it, out April 20, 2018.
